locator: I q.3 a.5 ad 2: Deus autem non est mensura proportionata alicui. Dicitur tamen mensura omnium, ex eo quod unumquodque tantum habet de esse, quantum ei appropinquat
interpretation: Order reading of the sentence that AQUINAS-ST-I-Q3-A5-AD2-MEASURE-BY-APPROACH-A reads as stated. 'Tantum habet de esse, quantum ei appropinquat' is read as a biconditional: one thing is more a being than another exactly when it approaches the measure more nearly (degrees of approach in their own preorder). 'Non est mensura proportionata' and 'appropinquat' are read as strict primacy: everything other than the measure approaches it less nearly than the measure itself stands, so the measure is not one more grade among the measured. Strict primacy is a reading choice (DISAMB-ORDER-OF-BEING): the sentence does not say in so many words that nothing ties with God, and the results show the clause is load-bearing. The primary is a parameter; that it is God comes from the sentence's subject and is not formalized. Nothing in the sentence says that the measure causes what it measures.
